content.thinking: I should keep my response to just one sentence.

action_items.item: Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after it was switched off in the flag provider, and fix it.
Alert when the state the flag provider holds for a flag differs from the state io-shop logs it evaluating.
Switch monthly-spend-feature off, confirm from io-shop's own evaluation logs that it is off, and keep it off until the proposed fix is merged.
Make the Mitigation Agent confirm from the service's own evaluations that a flag revert took effect before it judges the revert refuted and puts the flag back.
Turn monthly-spend-feature on for a small share of shoppers first, before turning it on for everyone.
Add an automatic halt that turns a flag rollout back when the account page error rate climbs after the flag changes.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's share of failed requests rose from {errors_before} before the onset to a peak of {errors_at_worst}. The service's own logs put the account page error rate at typically {Gbac1.6}, reaching {Gbac1.5} at {Gbac1.7}.

Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error was logged throughout {G5309.3} and did not appear in the logs read from before the onset.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the change events read for the day before the onset and after it came back with flag changes only, and no deploys.
The ClientDisconnected account page failures: they were already logged before the onset, while account pages were rendering normally.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. Before that the service evaluated the flag as off and account pages rendered normally. At {G971b.6}, {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations came back on, and from then on every evaluation logged was on.

With the flag on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides this month's total by the number of this month's purchases. For shoppers who have bought before but not this month, that number is empty, so the division raises and serve_account_page fails the request.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly spending summary sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought before but not this month, because it divides by the number of their purchases this month and they have none.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that covers the monthly spend summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. By Code-Fix's reading, the test cases it adds for that case would raise against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division fault would likely have been caught before anyone switched the flag on, so turning it on would not have broken account pages.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for every evaluation almost at once. No staged rollout, and no automatic halt tied to the account page error rate, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A smaller share of shoppers would have hit the failure, or the rollout would have stopped by itself once account page errors climbed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: Switching monthly-spend-feature off in the flag provider did not change what the service evaluated: its logs went on showing the flag as on after the switch-off at {P2.1}, through {Gce95.4}.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The revert of the flag would likely have stopped the failing account pages soon after it was made, instead of being judged ineffective.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been brought in while the failures went on, and could have taken up the flag that would not switch off once the automated revert did not help.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well: The Investigator named the switch-on of monthly-spend-feature as the candidate cause C1, {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
To test C1, the Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature off, {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
On its second pass, the Investigator noted in C2 that the logs still showed the flag on after the switch-off, which Gce95 bears out.
Code-Fix opened draft pull request PR #371, {T36.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent judged the flag revert REFUTED and switched monthly-spend-feature back on. The service's own logs show it never stopped evaluating the flag as on after the switch-off, so the revert was never really tested.
Argus moved to FIXING with no explanation left to try. C2 had pointed out that the flag kept evaluating on after the switch-off, but why the switch-off did not take effect was not followed up.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides account.total_this_month_cents by the length of the shopper's list of current-month purchases. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py and serve_account_page fails the account page request.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature back on, the division fault still in the code, and the service not seen to stop evaluating the flag as on when it was switched off, account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month would likely keep failing.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
